rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. This tests a simple RNA-only model with PCA encoding (singleprofile), isolating the RNA modality's performance. It clarifies the baseline accuracy and helps determine if multimodal approaches are necessary, aligning with exploration principles.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (same RNA encoder, no image encoder) to evaluate if profile setting improvements can boost accuracy. It isolates the effect of profile aggregation, providing critical evidence for whether multiprofile configurations outperform singleprofile ones, which is a key design choice with uncertain impact.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002: 0.5907 accuracy) outperforms singleprofile (config_001: 0.4849). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (config_002) with transformer aggregation in multiprofile RNA-only models improves accuracy, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of multiprofile's promise with exploration of transformer's potential, avoiding redundant changes to RNA encoder or profile setting.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.590664 accuracy) outperforms singleprofile and transformer aggregation. This experiment tests replacing PCA with scvi_n200 RNA encoder in the multiprofile/avgpool setup to isolate the effect of RNA encoder quality. It balances exploitation of the promising multiprofile setting with exploration of a potentially better encoder, while keeping other parameters consistent to attribute performance changes directly to the RNA encoder.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6501). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (config_006) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It is the best next step to exploit the promising scvi_n200 encoder and multiprofile setting while exploring a critical design choice.

The existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006, 0.653 accuracy) are the strongest so far. This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to the best RNA encoder with transformer aggregation, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It balances exploitation (building on the best RNA-only model) and exploration (testing multimodal potential), which could reveal if combining modalities improves accuracy further.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and resnet50 encoders (e.g., config_032) achieve high accuracy (0.6878). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion in the same architecture improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best use of the remaining budget to exploit the promising multimodal direction while refining key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a more advanced model) while keeping the same image encoder, aggregation, and fusion strategy could further improve performance. This directly compares two key RNA encoders under the same proven setup, clarifying whether scgpt offers incremental gains. It balances exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of a critical design choice.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l image encoder while keeping the high-performing transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. This clarifies whether the stronger image encoder (vit_l) can further improve accuracy, directly comparing key design choices in a controlled manner.

Existing evidence shows config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (config_051) could improve performance, isolating the effect of RNA encoder choice. It's the best use of the final experiment to explore a critical design choice with minimal changes, leveraging the strong prior evidence for multimodal and weighted fusion.
